rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the same core real issues (RuixiangMa missing from diffusion/models, LoRA narrowing mislabeled as 'preserved', offloader.md/PR-description mismatch on Isotr0py, plugins rule contradicting its cited doc, distributed/ broader than its doc), giving comparable recall against the ground-truth set (most of which was already resolved by the shown diff). X reads as more polished and gives richer prose fixes, but it asserts unverifiable specifics (precise per-directory blast-radius file counts, invented-looking commit SHAs/PR numbers) without evidence trails, which is a real fabrication risk and hurts precision. Y ties nearly every claim to a quoted file:line or tool output (gh_pr_view/gh_ci_read/file_at_base) and systematically cross-checks PR-body claims against the diff — closely mirroring the Copilot-style 'doc says X but file says Y' findings in the ground truth — though its 'Additional observations' section is marred by several sentences cut off mid-word, denting actionability there.
